Here is what the market is arguing about as of 8:55 AM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-24. The sources disagree with each other in places and some figures are unusually large, so I flag where the numbers are shaky.

**1. Is the AI-chip rebound real? (the dominant story)**
- The S&P 500 fell for seven straight sessions, its longest streak since February 2020, and closed Friday in correction territory. It was down about 11.6% from its October record, and the Nasdaq is negative for the year. The VIX was around 37.
- Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday. He had stepped down on Nov. 12 after admitting to an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia jumped 31.5% on Monday, and Micron, AMD, Oracle and CoreWeave rallied with it.
- Monday was the biggest one-day gain since April 2025. The Nasdaq rose about 6.5%, the S&P 500 about 4.7% and the Dow about 3%.
- This morning futures are giving some of it back. Nasdaq-100 futures are down about 1.2%, S&P 500 futures about 0.5% and Dow futures about 0.1%. Nvidia is down roughly 3.5% to 5.4% premarket.
- The debate is whether this is a relief squeeze or the end of the selloff. Open worries are scrutiny of Nvidia's China chip sales and national-security risk.

**2. AI server demand and margins**
- HPE fell about 10% premarket after warning about margins in its cloud and AI business. Semtech is also lower.
- Dell reports after the close today, and it is the next test of whether AI hardware makers can keep their margins.
- Also reporting today: HP Inc., Autodesk, Workday and Analog Devices.

**3. The Fed may hike, not cut**
- Rate-hike expectations are the backdrop for stocks. The Fed hiked in September and held in October. CME FedWatch shows over 90% odds of a quarter-point hike on Dec. 9, and Treasury yields are elevated.
- Governor Waller said the Fed may need to "shock people" with a half-point hike. The minutes showed almost all officials expect more hikes.
- Core PCE inflation is due Wednesday, expected at about 3.2% year over year. It is the last inflation reading before the meeting.
- One source said traders have stopped fully pricing a December hike. That conflicts with the others, so check the current FedWatch odds.

**4. The consumer and the holiday**
- Dick's Sporting Goods rose about 18% premarket on a Q3 beat and 2026 sales outlook, and Dollar Tree also gained. Best Buy and Kohl's report this morning.
- The question for Best Buy is how rising memory prices are hurting electronics demand. Intel's weak PC guidance adds to that worry.
- Markets are closed Thursday and close at 1 PM ET (12:00 PM CT) Friday. Black Friday spending data is the next consumer signal.

**5. Deals and sectors**
- Insmed jumped after Sanofi agreed to buy it for about $41 billion.
- Agilent rose on an earnings beat, and Fluence Energy rose on a record backlog.

**6. Oil and geopolitics**
- Brent is about $89 and WTI about $80, near three-month lows on oversupply. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, which gives oil some support.

**7. Overseas**
- Japan's Nikkei rose 3.9% and the Topix 2.5%, following the US rally. The Hang Seng fell 0.7%.

**Caveats**
- Some live-blog snapshots showed the S&P 500 down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq down 1.8%. Another showed the S&P 500 up 0.3%. Those timestamps probably differ, so treat intraday levels as unsettled.
- I read two articles in full (TipRanks and CNBC). The rest comes from search summaries.

**ANF: what happened and what could move it (Tuesday 2026-11-24, about 8:55 AM CT)**

**The story.** ANF reported fiscal Q3 (ended Oct 31) before the open and beat clearly. The raise looks mostly operational, not a one-off.

- **Sales:** $1.435B, up 11%, against about $1.37B expected. Comparable sales rose 6%. Abercrombie brands grew 12% and Hollister 11%. APAC was up 24%, EMEA 12% and the Americas 11%.
- **Profit:** EPS was $3.82 against about $3.08–$3.15 expected, and $2.36 a year ago. Operating margin was 15.5% against 12.0%.
- **Quality of the beat:** Average selling price (AUR) rose high single digits. Inventory was up only about 4%, and management called it "appropriately positioned". Traffic was described as stable.
- **One-offs:** About $20M of tariff refunds (IEEPA) added $0.40 to EPS. That is roughly half of the $0.73 beat, or about a quarter of the $1.39 year-over-year gain. Excluding it, EPS was about $3.42, still well above consensus.
- **Guidance:**
  - Full-year EPS was raised to $13.70–$13.90 from $13.10–$13.60. About $2.15 of that is refunds.
  - Q4 guide is sales up about 7%, operating margin about 15%, and EPS $4.40–$4.60.
  - Buybacks are at least $120M in Q4 and at least $500M for the year.
  - Management cited a strong start to November, with the biggest weeks still ahead. That makes the Q4 guide look conservative, though they didn't call it that.
- **Setup before today:** The stock already jumped about 37% on the Q2 report in August, when $100M of tariff refunds drove the beat. That is why the old high was $172.00, and the stock is now near it.

**What could move it over the next few sessions**

- **Upside:**
  - Analyst target raises should come today and tomorrow. Before the report, MarketBeat's consensus target was $159.71. Jefferies was at $175 and BMO at $170, and both are now below or near the price, so they should be revised up.
  - The stock trades at about 11–12x forward earnings, even at $172.
  - Holiday data this week, with Thanksgiving on Nov 26 and Black Friday, could reinforce the "strong November" comment.
  - Buybacks add steady demand.
- **Downside:**
  - The move is extended: +22.7% on the day and 12 times normal volume, with the stock at the 52-week high. Gap-and-fade is a real risk, and some profit-taking is likely.
  - Citi downgraded the stock to Neutral in August on the non-recurring refunds. Morgan Stanley is Equal Weight. Zacks cut its rating on Nov 9.
  - The refunds won't repeat. Management expects no more refunds. It also said freight is about 100 bps worse than the August guide, and incentive pay will normalize in 2027. There is no 2027 guide until March.
  - Analysts expect revenue growth to slow to about 4%, from 11% this quarter.
  - Insiders sold about $6M in August. I found no purchases.
  - Short-interest figures conflict (8–16% of float), so I can't say whether a squeeze helped today's move.
- **Sector:** XRT context matters, since the stock is 20% ahead of it today. I found no 2026 holiday or apparel-specific data.

**Read for the journal.** The fundamentals back the gap: a broad beat, real pricing power, clean inventory, and a Q4 guide that looks beatable. The risk for a 1–10 session hold is entry price. The stock is up 22.7% on 12 times volume, at the high, and the refund-driven EPS and 2027 questions give skeptics an argument once the first rush fades. **Agilent (A): research summary, 8:55 AM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-24**

**The story.** Agilent beat on the fiscal Q4 report and guided FY27 above consensus. The stock gapped to an all-time high on that guide, and the Street is raising targets.

**What was reported (Agilent's 8-K press release, 11-23):**
- **Q4 revenue:** $2.04B, up 9.6% reported and 8.3% core. It's the first quarter above $2B and beat the $1.98–2.00B guide.
- **Q4 EPS:** non-GAAP $1.86, up 17%, against a $1.71–1.74 guide and a consensus of about $1.72–1.73.
- **Tariff refunds:** they added $0.07 to Q4 EPS and about 120 bp to margin. Ex-refund EPS was about $1.79, which is still a beat.
- **Segments:** Life Sciences and Diagnostics $843M (+12%), CrossLab services $799M (+6%), Applied Markets $398M (+13%).
- **FY26 totals:** revenue $7.55B, non-GAAP EPS $6.34.
- **FY27 guide:** revenue $8.00–8.15B (core +5–7%), EPS $6.73–6.86. Consensus was about $7.99B and $6.70. Management cited a "clear path" to the high end if momentum holds.
- **Q1 FY27 guide:** revenue $1.96–2.00B and EPS $1.54–1.57, above consensus of about $1.93B and $1.50 (FactSet, via TipRanks). Neither outlook includes future tariff refunds.
- **FY27 cash items:** capex about $450M and operating cash flow $2.0–2.1B.
- **Capital returns:** no new buyback or dividend news.

**Call detail (Investing.com summary, not a transcript):**
- **China:** grew 19% in Q4, with pharma above 40%.
  - FY27 assumes mid-single-digit growth, with a flat first half and mid-teens in the second half.
  - Management put the SAMR stimulus at about $40–45M, with Agilent capturing roughly 30–33% of it, mostly in Q1.
  - I could not confirm the SAMR program from any independent source.
- **Pharma and CDMO:**
  - Pharma grew 9%, and FY27 guides to high-single-digit growth.
  - The CDMO unit (Advanced Therapeutics) is guided to mid-teens growth in FY27, weighted to the second half.
  - Trains A and B are near full, and Train C starts in spring 2027, with about a 30 bp margin drag in FY27.
- **Reshoring:** about a $300M opportunity over 3–4 years. Five of the top 10 pharma companies had placed early orders, per the Q3 report.
- **Other demand:**
  - Management said the liquid-chromatography replacement cycle is "not yet halfway."
  - PFAS testing grew more than 60%.
  - Direct AI and semiconductor exposure is only 3–4% of revenue.

**Analysts (Benzinga and TipRanks, via search results).** Before the report the average target was about $183–185. Since then:
- Leerink $210 (from $170)
- Baird $208 (from $195)
- RBC $205 (from $185)
- Citi $205 (from $190), Buy
- Stifel and TD Cowen $205
- Evercore $200 (from $178)

Premarket the stock hit about $188, above the old all-time high. Options had priced about a 10% move, and it moved roughly 6–7%, so the move was no bigger than the options market implied.

**What could move it over the next 1–10 sessions:**
- **Upside:**
  - More target raises and upgrades as models update.
  - Strong sector tape.
  - Follow-through from a clean beat and raise, with a stock now at a new high and well above its averages.
- **Downside and fade risks:**
  - **Valuation:** about 34.5x trailing earnings (Trefis, October; Investing.com's P/E of 34.6 is on a similar basis), and the stock is already above many of the new targets' midpoints. Several targets sit only 8–12% above $187.
  - **Quality of the beat:** part of the EPS beat came from the tariff refund.
  - **Q1 EPS:** the Q1 guide of $1.54–1.57 is below Q4's $1.86 (and below $1.79 ex-refund), which skeptics may point to.
  - **Back-half weighting:** FY27 growth is expected to be stronger in the first half and slower in the second against tougher comparisons.
  - **Costs:** Train C startup costs, memory chip costs and Middle East logistics.
  - **Stretched run-up:** the stock was already up about 14% from the August raise, and gap-ups to all-time highs after a big run can retrace.
- **Calendar:** I found no scheduled company catalyst over the next few sessions. Thanksgiving week brings thin volume.

**Read:** this is a fundamentally clean beat and raise with a real driver (China, pharma, CDMO), not a one-off. It is also an expensive stock with a lot already priced in. The case for continued drift is analyst momentum. The case against is the premium multiple and the stock being above most of the new price targets.

**Bottom line:** The gap-up has solid fundamentals behind it, but the stock has already moved up to the level analysts had as a target. The quarter was a relief rally and not a clean beat. The next few sessions depend on whether the stock holds the gap and whether analysts chase it.

**What happened.** Dick's reported Q3 (quarter ended Oct 31) before the open today. I read the company's 8-K press release and the Investing.com call-transcript summary.
- Sales were $5.13B, up 23.2%, mostly from the Foot Locker acquisition. Consensus was about $5.06B to $5.08B.
- Adjusted EPS was $1.94, against about $1.38 to $1.42 expected. It was down from $2.07 a year ago. GAAP EPS was $1.87, up from $0.86.
- Comps (same-store sales):

| Business | Q3 comp | Year-ago comp |
|---|---|---|
| DICK'S | +2.6% | +5.7% |
| Foot Locker (pro forma) | +0.5% | -4.7% |
| Consolidated (pro forma) | +1.8% | +1.7% |

- The Dick's comp slowed from 4.9% in Q2, and management blamed warm October weather for cold-weather categories. The Foot Locker comp was the first positive print since the deal.
- U.S. Foot Locker comps were up over 4%, helped by Jordan launches and Caitlin Clark product. Europe, Middle East and Africa is the weak region. Management called it "a longer slog."
- The full-year adjusted EPS guide rose to $11.45 to $12.30, from $11.00 to $12.00. The Dick's comp floor rose to +3.3% to +4.0%, and Dick's segment operating income to $1.56B to $1.61B. Foot Locker guidance was unchanged: comps of -2% to 0% and an operating loss of $40M to $80M.
- Dick's bought back 6.7M shares for $903M in the quarter at an average of about $135, and $2.12B of authorization remains. Q4 is modeled on about 83M shares, so buybacks lift EPS.

**Why the stock is up.** The setup was bleak. The stock fell about 31% in a day in August on a guidance cut, was down about 32% on the year before today, and had about 18% of its float sold short (ZeroHedge). A beat, a raised guide and Foot Locker growth forced shorts to cover. Coverage had it as the biggest one-day gain since April 2020.

**What could move it over the next one to ten sessions**
- **Analyst targets.** Bloomberg-tracked analysts' average 12-month target is about $160, and the stock is at $154. A wave of raises would support it, and so would more short covering. If targets sit near $160, upside from here is limited.
- **Gap fill.** The stock is still below its 200-day average ($185) and its 50-day average is falling. That is overhead supply, and sellers could use this rally to exit. The prior close was about $133.7.
- **Quality of the beat.** Adjusted EPS fell year over year, and gross margin fell 73 basis points to 32.4%, mostly from Foot Locker mix. Management said Q3 was the margin low point. Foot Locker still lost $40.9M in the quarter.
- **Holiday read-through.** No quarter-to-date comp figures were disclosed. Foot Locker inventory is up 16%, and clearance runs through 2027. Nike's Jordan reset is a near-term headwind for Foot Locker. Retail data and Black Friday reads could move the stock either way.
- **Guidance.** No 2027 guidance was given. It is tentatively due March 9, 2027. Management flagged freight, fuel and occupancy inflation for 2027.

The search returned only older years, so the $160 average target comes from one Bloomberg-sourced article. I found no current short-interest figure beyond that same article. Several aggregator sites mixed up fiscal years. The consensus EPS I used ($1.38 to $1.42) comes from Finviz and Investing.com. One aggregator showed a conflicting $2.71 consensus, which I discarded. - **Financial conditions are tightening.** The minutes cite wider credit spreads for riskier and AI-related borrowers, higher mortgage rates, and less high-yield issuance. Wells Fargo was the weakest against estimates, per StockStory. Higher rates help net interest income, but they also raise credit, deposit-cost and securities-loss worries. That implies about $54 per TRMK share, an 18.6% premium, at 1.78x tangible book. HWC holders would own about 65% of the combined bank, which would have about $58B in assets across six states. The close is expected in late Q1 2027, pending regulators and both shareholder votes. ([release](https://finviz.com/news/421671/hancock-whitney-corporation-to-acquire-trustmark-corporation), [Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/hancock-whitney-buy-trustmark-3b-deal-bank-acquisition/874522/))
- **The terms:** Management says the deal is about 7% accretive to 2028 EPS. It is also about 7% dilutive to tangible book value, with a roughly 2.8-year earn-back, and mildly dilutive to regulatory capital. Expected savings are $205.5M pre-tax. Merger costs were modeled at about $250M pre-tax. ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-hancock-whitney-stock-sliding-today-93CH-5023071), [Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/hancock-whitney-buy-trustmark-3b-deal-bank-acquisition/874522/))

HWC had closed the One Florida Bank (OFB) deal on Aug 1 and had just spent much of its excess capital. ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-hancock-whitney-nasdaq-hwc-shares-gap-down-heres-why-2026-11-12/), [Rallies](https://rallies.ai/news/hancock-whitney-shares-fall-after-32-billion-trustmark-deal-29d2e751fb6272bd))

- Each Zscaler share converts to 1.135 CRWD shares, a 34% premium. CRWD holders end up with about 84% of the combined company.
- Management cites about $1B of added annual revenue within 30 months and $500M of cost savings. The CFO says it is immediately accretive to free cash flow per share before synergies.
